comments.content: The `guidance` state has no subscription to refresh itself when the stored value changes from elsewhere. The analogous `showTasks` state in this same component pairs with `WORKFLOW_VISIBILITY_EVENT` (defined in `workflowVisibility.ts`, emitted inside `setShowWorkflowTasks()`) precisely for cross-webview / cross-component sync, and is also re-read in `App.tsx` and `WidgetApp.tsx`. `workflowPrompt.ts` (added in this batch) does NOT emit any equivalent event after `setDecomposeGuidance()` or `resetDecomposeGuidance()` — both silently write to localStorage. If any other call site ever writes to that key (a future "import preset" button, devtools reset, test setup, the widget window, or a second SettingsPage instance), this textarea will display stale content until the component remounts, and the user will happily edit on top of a value they cannot see. Mirror the `workflowVisibility` contract — add an event constant exported from `workflowPrompt.ts`, `emit()` it from `setDecomposeGuidance()` / `resetDecomposeGuidance()`, and `listen()` here to call `setGuidance(getDecomposeGuidance())`.

Persistence is wired exclusively to the textarea's `onBlur`. If the textarea is unmounted (route change, panel collapse, widget window close) or the page is reloaded while focus still sits in the field, the in-memory `guidance` is silently dropped — no `useEffect` cleanup flushes the value, no explicit save button exists, and no app-wide `beforeunload` guard fires (confirmed: zero `beforeunload` references in the repo). Compared with the visibility toggle right above (which writes synchronously on click), the new control has a noticeably weaker durability story for the same card. Either add a small `useEffect(() => () => { if (!guidanceSaved) setDecomposeGuidance(guidance); }, [guidance, guidanceSaved])` cleanup to flush on unmount, or switch to a debounced auto-save on change so the save indicator stops being load-bearing for data integrity.

The prompt textarea has no length cap and shows no character / token feedback, yet its value is forwarded verbatim to the LLM in `workflow_decompose.rs` (added in this batch). A user pasting a multi-thousand-character guide will see no warning before "AI 生成"; any downstream failure (context overflow, fence/JSON validation failure that the validation chain reports back as a retry) surfaces later with no obvious cause pointing at prompt size. `setDecomposeGuidance()` in `workflowPrompt.ts` accepts any string with no upper bound. Consider at minimum a soft `maxLength` (e.g., ~2000 chars to keep it well under typical 8K-context budget after the contract segment is appended) plus a small `length / maxLength` counter under the textarea; the existing `nm-inset` text style already used for the textarea will match the rest of the card.

comments.content: The catch comment "localStorage 不可用：仅本次会话内存生效" is misleading: the value isn't kept in any memory either — it's silently discarded. Consider rewording to something like "localStorage 不可用：本次写入不持久化，下次读取仍返回旧值或默认值" to match actual behavior.

The toolbar "重新生成" button (and its `regenerate()` handler) is not gated by `activeId !== null`, but the button's title and the `EmptyHero` regenerate copy both promise "当前画布在保存前保持不变" / "重新生成工作流". A user who just hit "创建空白工作流" (`createBlank` sets `activeId = null`, line 147) can still click 重新生成 twice and end up in `mode === "hero"`, where `isRegenerate={activeId !== null}` (line 573) is false → `EmptyHero` renders the "新建工作流" variant, not the "重新生成工作流" variant, contradicting the button's promise. Either hide the button (mirroring the `{activeId && <delete/>}` pattern at line 551) or gate `regenerate()` on `activeId !== null`.

Default-name detection by string-comparing `prev` against `\`工作流 ${new Date().toLocaleDateString()}\`` is fragile: the same format is produced by `createBlank` (line 148) at a different wall-clock instant, so any regeneration that crosses midnight / DST / a timezone shift will mismatch and the stale default name is kept (defeating the intent to refresh). Store an explicit `isNameDefault` flag (or compute the default lazily inside the updater against `savedSnapshot`) instead of reverse-engineering it from a date string.
comments.existing_code: setName((prev) => (prev && prev !== `工作流 ${new Date().toLocaleDateString()}` ? prev : goalText.slice(0, 12)));

comments.content: Magic number `12` truncates the goal-derived workflow name; CJK characters are counted the same as ASCII, so `goalText.slice(0, 12)` silently cuts "汇总并邮件通知本周完成的任务" to "汇总并邮件通知本周完". Hoist the limit to a named constant (e.g. `NAME_FROM_GOAL_MAX_CHARS`) — preferably with `.chars().count()` — so it is consistent with the `MAX_NODE_TITLE` cap used in the backend validator and any future locale change is a single-line edit.

comments.content: The bottom of `EmptyHero` now nests two state-dependent branches (`decomposing ? <cancel/> : <>...two buttons</>`) inside an already-multi-prop component; this is the densest JSX block in the file. Extracting a small `EmptyHeroActions` subcomponent (or a `renderActions()` helper that takes `decomposing / onDecompose / onCancelDecompose / isRegenerate / goal`) would make the conditional structure flat and easier to test in isolation.

The "已保存" indicator has no auto-hide mechanism. `guidanceSaved` flips to `true` on `onBlur` and only resets to `false` on the next keystroke or when the reset button is clicked. Once a user has saved once, the label stays visible permanently for the rest of the session even though it is meant to be a transient confirmation — readers will perceive it as static chrome rather than feedback. Add a short timer (or clear it on a subsequent interaction) so the indicator fades after a few seconds, mirroring the affordance users expect from save-toasts.

No trim/empty guard before persisting. The user can clear the textarea (or fill it with whitespace only) and tab away; the empty/whitespace string is written to localStorage and subsequently forwarded verbatim to the LLM by `workflow_decompose.rs`. Trim the value and fall back to the default before writing, or at minimum block the save when the trimmed value is empty so a stale default can't be silently replaced with garbage.

`setDecomposeGuidance` swallows localStorage errors silently (see `workflowPrompt.ts` try/catch), but the UI unconditionally flips `guidanceSaved` to `true` and shows "已保存". When storage is unavailable (private mode quota exceeded, storage disabled, etc.) the user gets a false confirmation and the next "AI 生成" call will still use the prior value. Either have `setDecomposeGuidance` return a success boolean and surface a failure message here, or drop the misleading indicator when storage is unavailable.

The `guidance` parameter is not length-capped before being concatenated into `system_prompt`. Compare with `goal`, which is bounded by `MAX_WORKFLOW_GOAL` (500) earlier in this function: a user (or a SettingsPage.tsx textarea with no `maxLength` attribute) can paste an arbitrarily large prompt, which is then billed on every LLM call and may blow past the model's context window. Add a symmetric `MAX_DECOMPOSE_GUIDANCE` constant in `db/workflow.rs` (e.g. a few KB) and reject longer input with `CommandError::InvalidArgument` just like `goal` does.

The retry loop has no overall deadline. `summarize_http` (bot_chat.rs) sets a per-request 60s timeout, but this loop runs up to 2 attempts back-to-back, so the command can block for ~120s before returning. Combined with no cancellation propagation — the frontend `cancelDecompose` only increments `decomposeSeqRef` (WorkflowPage.tsx), it does not abort the in-flight Tauri command — a user who clicks "取消" still pays for the second attempt. Either bound the loop with a wall-clock deadline (e.g. `tokio::time::timeout` around the whole loop) or skip the retry if `summarize_messages` returns a transient/infra error vs. a validation error.

The duplicate-title suffix scheme is greedy and not collision-safe. `seen` is keyed on the *current* (possibly already-suffixed) title, so input `["审阅", "审阅", "审阅（2）"]` produces `["审阅", "审阅（2）", "审阅（2）"]` — two tasks with the same display name. The unit test `validate_suffixes_duplicate_titles` only covers the all-identical-input case. Either key `seen` on the *original* (pre-suffix) title, or normalize input titles by stripping an existing `（n）` suffix before counting.

The Tauri command `workflow_decompose` itself has no test coverage. All 8 new unit tests target only the helper functions (`parse_and_validate`, `validate_decompose`, `build_system_prompt`); the retry-and-feedback path, the error-feedback string format (`你上一次的输出未通过校验：…请严格按照输出格式要求重新输出 JSON。`), and the audit event payload (`("subtasks", n)`, `("attempts", n)`) are exercised only by hand. `summarize_http` already exposes a `pub` seam for tests (bot_chat.rs:1022) — consider wiring an integration test that drives the full command with a mock client so the retry/audit contract is locked down.

The hardcoded contract tells the model "subtasks：1 到 20 个元素" but the validator caps at `MAX_WORKFLOW_NODES = 30`. Either tighten the contract to match the validator (preferred — `MAX_WORKFLOW_NODES` is the source of truth from `db/workflow.rs`) or document the deliberate looseness. Right now the contract overpromises for up to 10 extra elements that the model could emit and the validator would still accept.

comments.content: Audit event is only emitted on success. After both retries fail (the `break` path on line 235), the function returns `CommandError::Internal(...)` without ever calling `audit::write_event`. For an LLM-driven command that consumes API quota and runs over user-supplied `goal`, failed attempts should be audited at least at Warn/Error level (event name `workflow_decompose_failed`, with `attempts`/`reason` kv) so the bot.log shows whether a user keeps hitting validation errors, vs. transient LLM flakiness. The success path on line 221 is the only audit call.

For an LLM-driven command that consumes API quota and runs over user-supplied `goal`, failed attempts should be audited at least at Warn/Error level (e.g. event `workflow_decompose_failed`, with `attempts`/`reason` kv) so bot.log distinguishes persistent validation errors from transient LLM flakiness. The success branch on line 221 is the only audit call in this command.

Race: in-flight AI decompose response can overwrite later state changes. `openWorkflow` (line 124), `createBlank` (line 145), and `addNode` (line 208) don't bump `decomposeSeqRef.current`, so the guard `if (seq !== decomposeSeqRef.current) return;` in `runDecompose` (line 171) still passes after the user navigates away. Concrete data-loss path: user is on `EmptyHero`, clicks "AI 生成" → LLM in flight → user clicks a "已有工作流" chip → `openWorkflow` sets nodes from the loaded workflow and `setMode("edit")` → LLM returns and `setNodes(fresh)` silently overwrites the loaded workflow's nodes (with `setSavedSnapshot(null)` marking it dirty) → next save overwrites the loaded workflow on the server. `openWorkflow`/`createBlank`/`addNode` should all increment `decomposeSeqRef.current` (mirroring how they already bump `openSeqRef.current`) before kicking off their own async/state work.

`createBlank` must also bump `decomposeSeqRef.current` for the same reason as `openWorkflow` — otherwise a slow LLM response that arrives after `createBlank` finishes will replace the brand-new blank canvas with AI-generated nodes (and the user just saw the "create blank" confirmation). The pattern is already established here for `openSeqRef`; just add the decompose counter too.

`addNode` should also cancel an in-flight decompose. From `EmptyHero`, while `decomposing` is true the textarea is disabled and the user has no path forward — but the toolbar "加卡" button is still enabled in hero mode, so a user can click it, then watch their single node get silently replaced when the LLM response arrives. Either disable "加卡" while `decomposing`, or bump `decomposeSeqRef.current` inside `addNode` so the arriving response is discarded like other navigation paths.

Tooltips/aria on the armed toolbar button: the visual state flips between "重新生成" and "确认重生成？" but the button has no `aria-pressed` to communicate the armed state to assistive tech (the `title` is read on hover, not on focus-announce). While touching the file, add `aria-pressed={regenArmed}` so screen-reader users get the same cue sighted users do.

comments.content: `regenArmed` and its 3 s timer leak across navigation. The `新建` button on line 509 just calls `setMode("hero")` and the workflow dropdown's `onChange` calls `openWorkflow`/`createBlank` — none of them clear `regenArmed` or `armedTimerRef`. After a user clicks 重新生成 once (arming), if they then click 新建 or switch the dropdown, the toolbar still shows "确认重生成？" until the original timer fires. Either gate `regenArmed` on the same condition as the second click (active workflow present), or have those navigation paths reset it. The 重新生成 button itself is `disabled={decomposing}` only, so the armed visual also lingers across mode changes.

The `新建` button on line 509 just calls `setMode("hero")`, and the workflow `select` on line 490's `onChange` calls `openWorkflow`/`createBlank` — none of them clear `regenArmed` or `armedTimerRef`. So if the user arms 重新生成 (first click → "确认重生成？" armed), then clicks 新建 or picks a different workflow in the dropdown, the toolbar still shows "确认重生成？" with the original 3 s timer running until it fires. Suggested fix: extract a small `resetRegenArmed()` helper (clears timer + `setRegenArmed(false)`) and call it from `openWorkflow`, `createBlank`, and the `setMode("hero")` click — i.e., every path that leaves the regenerate flow.
